title: Quogue
summary: Quogue is recorded as a village in western Southampton on Quantuck Bay. The name is a shortened form of Quaquanantuck, the older name for the salt meadows and land in this section.
history_content: Town records preserve several shortened spellings for the Quogue tract in the eighteenth century. The broader Quogue purchase and Quaquanantuck landscape are represented in the related Quantuck and Quaquanantuck record.
translation_content:
Quogue is not derived from the Narragansett word for round clam. It is treated here as a shortened form of Quaquanantuck, interpreted as a cove or estuary where the land or water quakes or trembles.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are links to the past, mirrors reflecting various scenarios and activities of the past.”

— Marcas Mac Coinnigh, Memory and Landscape (2026), Opening discussion

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: Quogue shows how a long Indigenous placename was shortened into the modern village name while still carrying the older meadow, bay, and purchase history of western Southampton.
